'''GNOME Keyring''' is a software application designed to store security credentials such as [[User (computing)|usernames]],<ref name="pro-opensolaris"/> [[password]]s,<ref name="pro-opensolaris"/> and [[Public-key cryptography|keys]], together with a small amount of relevant [[metadata]]. The sensitive data is [[encrypt]]ed and stored in a keyring [[computer file|file]] in the user's [[home directory]]. The default keyring uses the login [[password]] for encryption, so users don't need to remember another password.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://askubuntu.com/tags/gnome-keyring/info|title='gnome-keyring' tag wiki - Ask Ubuntu|access-date=28 February 2017}}</ref>

As of 2009, GNOME Keyring was part of the desktop environment in the operating system [[OpenSolaris]].<ref name="pro-opensolaris"/>

GNOME Keyring is implemented as a [[Daemon (computer software)|daemon]] and uses the [[Process (computing)|process]] name ''gnome-keyring-daemon''. Applications can store and request passwords by using the
''libsecret'' [[library (computing)|library]] which replaces the deprecated ''libgnome-keyring'' library.

GNOME Keyring is part of the [[GNOME]] desktop. As of 2006, it integrated with [[NetworkManager]] to store [[Wired Equivalent Privacy|WEP]] passwords.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HZ37FT3unW8C&dq=gnome-keyring&pg=PA161|page=161|title=Ubuntu Hacks: Tips & Tools for Exploring, Using, and Tuning Linux|year=2006|first1=Jonathan|last1=Oxer|first2=Kyle|last2=Rankin|first3=Bill|last3=Childers|publisher=[[O'Reilly Media]]|isbn=9780596551469}}</ref> [[GNOME Web]] and the email client [[Geary (software)|Geary]] uses GNOME Keyring to store passwords.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cqJoDwAAQBAJ&q=keyring |title=Beginning Modern Unix: Learn to Live Comfortably in a Modern Unix Environment |first=Manish |last=Jain |publisher=[[Apress]] |year=2018 |page=186|isbn=9781484235287 }}</ref>

On systems where GNOME Keyring is present, software written in [[Vala (programming language)|Vala]] can use it to store and retrieve passwords.<ref>{{cite book |title=Gnome 3 Application Development Beginner's Guide |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o4TnACjehLcC&q=keyring |first=Mohammad |last=Anwari |year=2013 |publisher=Packt Publishing Ltd|isbn = 9781849519434}}</ref> The GNOME Keyring Manager (gnome-keyring-manager) was the first user interface for the GNOME Keyring. As of GNOME 2.22, it is deprecated and replaced entirely with [[Seahorse (software)|Seahorse]].<ref>{{cite web
 | url   = https://help.gnome.org/misc/release-notes/2.22/
 | title = GNOME 2.22 Release Notes}}</ref>
